name: Dirichlet series of an arithmetic function
equivalent_forms: ordinary coefficient transform on the multiplicative monoid of positive integers
Mellin-type generating object for arithmetic coefficients

counterexamples.claim: Every formal Dirichlet series converges for all complex s
counterexamples.counterexample: zeta(s) does not converge as a series for Re(s)<=1

ant_to_pvg_map.map: n=prod p^{alpha_p} maps to alpha=nu(n); coefficient f(n) becomes a weight on finite-support valuation points and n^{-s}=prod p^{-s alpha_p}

pvg_geometric_object.object: weighted sum over the lattice of finite-support valuation vectors

pvg_to_ant_return_map.map: decode each labelled valuation vector to n and recover the coefficient term

loses: pointwise geometry after infinite summation unless coefficients are retained separately
claim_ceiling: Known generating-series language only; no analytic continuation or zero information is created.

name: Dirichlet convolution becomes product
conditions: absolute convergence sufficient to rearrange the double sum

ant_to_pvg_map.map: split each valuation vector alpha into beta+(alpha-beta); convolution over divisor boxes becomes Cauchy multiplication over lattice decompositions

loses: no loss at coefficient level; analytic rearrangement requires convergence hypotheses
claim_ceiling: Algebraic identity under stated convergence; not an asymptotic theorem.

name: Multiplicative arithmetic function
equivalent_forms: f is determined by its values on prime powers
on valuation vectors with disjoint supports, weight is multiplicative

counterexamples.claim: multiplicative means f(mn)=f(m)f(n) for all m,n

ant_to_pvg_map.map: f(alpha+beta)=f(alpha)f(beta) for disjoint-support valuation vectors alpha,beta

pvg_geometric_object.object: tensor factorization across independent prime axes

pvg_to_ant_return_map.map: decode disjoint-support vectors to coprime integers

claim_ceiling: Known structural equivalence; not a new classification theorem.

name: Euler product for a multiplicative function

conditions: absolute convergence in the asserted region

counterexamples.claim: Any arithmetic function has an Euler product
counterexamples.counterexample: a nonmultiplicative coefficient sequence need not factor into independent prime-axis local factors

ant_to_pvg_map.map: global valuation lattice sum factors as a product of one-dimensional sums along labelled prime axes

pvg_to_ant_return_map.map: multiply local prime-power generating factors and recover coefficients formally or analytically in the valid region

loses: global coefficient access becomes indirect after multiplication unless expanded
claim_ceiling: No zero-free region, continuation, or PNT consequence follows merely from writing the product.

conditions: Re(s)>1 for the series and Euler-product differentiation
pvg_interpretation: logarithmic differentiation converts independent local prime-axis factors into an additive prime-power weighted observable

prompt: Given tau, explain why its Dirichlet series is zeta(s)^2 and why tau is multiplicative but not completely multiplicative.
expected_route: tau is multiplicative because convolution of multiplicative functions is multiplicative
tau(4)=3 while tau(2)^2=4, so complete multiplicativity fails
PVG: local factor on one axis is sum_{k>=0}(k+1)x^k=(1-x)^{-2}
failure_modes: confusing Euler product with proof of PNT

claim: The Euler product alone proves the Prime Number Theorem
reason: The formal/local factorization encodes multiplicativity but PNT requires substantial analytic information such as a zero-free statement for zeta on Re(s)=1.
